papers.title: Synergistic enhancement of load-bearing and energy-absorbing performance in additively manufactured lattice structures through modifications to conventional unit cells
papers.abstract: The unit cell configuration of lattice structures critically influences their load-bearing and energy absorption performance. In this study, three novel lattice structures were developed by modifying the conventional FBCCZ unit cell through reversing, combining and turning strategies. The designed lattices were fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) using Ti-6Al-4V powder, and the mechanical properties, energy absorption capacity and deformation behaviors were systematically investigated through quasi-static compression tests and finite element simulations. The results demonstrate that the three modified lattices exhibit superior performance over the conventional FBCCZ structure in terms of fracture strain, specific yield strength, specific ultimate strength, specific energy absorption and energy absorption efficiency, thereby validating the efficacy of unit cell modifications in enhancing lattice performance. Notably, the CFBCCZ and TFBCCZ lattices significantly outperform both the FBCCZ and RFBCCZ lattice structures in load-bearing and energy absorption. While TFBCCZ shows marginally higher specific elastic modulus and energy absorption efficiency than CFBCCZ, the latter achieves superior energy absorption due to its highest ultimate strength and densification strain. Finite element simulations further reveal that the modified lattices, through optimized redistribution and adjustment of internal nodes and struts, effectively alleviate stress concentration during loading. This structural modification enhances the structural integrity and deformation stability under external loads, enabling a synergistic enhancement of load-bearing capacity and energy absorption performance.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究了激光粉末床熔融Ti-6Al-4V点阵结构的力学性能和能量吸收，属于该方向的基础力学范畴。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not investigate fatigue behavior, S-N curves, or crack initiation/propagation, which are core to the fatigue aspect of the direction focus.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过修改传统单胞设计来协同提升增材制造点阵结构的承载和吸能性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用反转、组合和转向策略设计三种新型点阵结构，利用LPBF制备Ti-6Al-4V试样并进行准静态压缩实验和有限元模拟。
summary_zh.result: 三种改性点阵结构在断裂应变、比强度、比能量吸收等方面均优于传统FBCCZ结构，其中CFBCCZ吸能最优。
summary_zh.validation: 通过准静态压缩实验与有限元模拟对比验证了改性结构的性能提升。

summary_en.motivation: To improve both load-bearing and energy absorption of additively manufactured lattice structures by modifying conventional unit cells.
summary_en.method: Three novel lattice structures were designed by reversing, combining, and turning the conventional FBCCZ unit cell, fabricated via LPBF using Ti-6Al-4V powder, and tested under quasi-static compression with finite element simulations.
summary_en.result: All three modified lattices outperformed the conventional FBCCZ in fracture strain, specific strength, and specific energy absorption, with CFBCCZ achieving the highest energy absorption.
summary_en.validation: Experimental quasi-static compression tests and finite element simulations validated the performance enhancement of the modified lattice designs.

papers.title: FINITE ELEMENT ANALYSIS AND TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZATION OF SLM ADDITIVE MANUFACTURED ORTHODONTIC BRACKETS
papers.abstract: With rising standards of living globally, restorative dentistry has gained popularity and increase the demand for high performance dental tools, such as dental bracket, implants. etc. However, conventional orthodontic bracket designs are constrained by the limitations of traditional manufacturing techniques, and often fail to optimize their designs, resulting in bulkier, less comfortable and efficient orthodontic appliances. This work explores the integration of topology optimization with additive manufacturing to design orthodontic brackets for enhanced performance and reduced mass. Finite element analysis (FEA) was conducted on 3D models of brackets made from five materials: Aluminum Oxide (Al2O3), Ferritic Stainless Steel, AISI 316L Stainless Steel, Titanium Alloy (Ti-6Al-4V), and Co-Cr Alloy. The brackets were subjected to a torque of 0.0294 N-m applied by a 0.483 mm x 0.483 mm archwire. The FEA results showed that only Ti-6Al-4V and Co-Cr alloys met the minimum safety factor requirement (>1), with safety factors of 1.85 and 1.89, respectively. Topology optimization was applied to minimize mass while maintaining a safety factor above 1.25. The optimized Ti-6Al-4V and Co-Cr brackets achieved a 46% mass reduction. Despite increased maximum stress and a slight decrease in safety factor, the optimized designs demonstrated the potential to withstand required torque levels with reduced material usage. Topology optimization was performed using the SIMP (Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization) method, with the objective of minimizing mass while maintaining a safety factor above 1.25.
papers.venue: International Journal of Modern Manufacturing Technologies

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文虽涉及Ti-6Al-4V材料，但主要聚焦于正畸托槽的结构设计与拓扑优化，而非Ti-6Al-4V增材制造的基础力学或疲劳性能表征。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on design optimization of orthodontic brackets using known material properties, not on characterizing the mechanical/fatigue behavior of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V. No experimental or computational study of Ti-6Al-4V's tensile, fatigue, or microstructural properties is presented.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用拓扑优化和增材制造设计高性能正畸托槽。
summary_zh.method: 对五种材料进行有限元分析和SIMP拓扑优化。
summary_zh.result: Ti-6Al-4V和Co-Cr合金满足安全要求并实现46%质量减少。
summary_zh.validation: 有限元模拟（无实验验证）。

summary_en.motivation: This work aims to improve orthodontic bracket design by integrating topology optimization and additive manufacturing to achieve reduced mass and enhanced performance.
summary_en.method: Finite element analysis was conducted on brackets made from five materials (including Ti-6Al-4V), and topology optimization using the SIMP method was applied to minimize mass while maintaining a safety factor above 1.25.
summary_en.result: Ti-6Al-4V and Co-Cr brackets met the safety requirements, achieving a 46% mass reduction after optimization without compromising structural integrity under applied torque.
summary_en.validation: The study relied solely on simulation; no experimental validation was performed.
